title.narrative: IDP and Famine Response for conflict Affected Persons in BNS

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtTo combat famine and reduce the risks of food insecurity in Blue Nile State (BNS), Samaritan’s Purse will develop a Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) and Livelihoods intervention in accordance with the SHF Reserve Allocation Strategy for Internally Displaced Person (IDP) and Famine Response. The proposed intervention aims to prevent famine in targeted communities by providing activities that augment food supply and improve livelihood means in the communities. This will be achieved through MPCA and a Livelihoods component which is aimed at building the resilience of communities, especially women and youth. The intervention will be integrated within Samaritan’s Purse’s ongoing Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL) projects in the hard-to-reach areas of BNS in order to maximize impact while avoiding duplication. The project will follow a layered approach with all services being provided to the same 5,000 IDP households (HHs) in BNS to optimize the fulfilment of beneficiaries’ needs.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtRegarding FSL, Samaritan’s Purse views livestock, as a source of high value protein, micronutrients and income, can significantly contribute to improving their nutritional status and overall health. Additionally, eggs provide a readily available and highly nutritious food source for young children.ltbrgtBy combining cash assistance, livestock distribution (goats and chickens), and capacity building, this project aims to:ltbrgtAddress immediate nutritional needs: Provide essential nutrients to pregnant women and children through livestock products.ltbrgtEnhance food security: Diversify income sources and reduce reliance on external food aid.ltbrgtEmpower women: Strengthen the economic position of FHHs.ltbrgtBuild resilience: Equip beneficiaries with the knowledge and skills to care for their livestock, ensuring long-term food security.ltbrgtStrengthen local capacity: Enhance the capacity of NCDO to respond to future livestock emergencies through Livestock Emergency Guidelines and Standards (LEGS) training.ltbrgtThese aims will be achieved through the distribution of small livestock (goats chickens) to 200 female headed HHs. The following activities will also be conducted under the FSL sector:ltbrgtDistribution of goats and poultry to the beneficiaries.ltbrgtTraining of the goat and poultry restocking beneficiaries on nutrition-sensitive agriculture and improved livestock production practices.ltbrgtProcurement of vaccines and accompanying drugs for the supportive antibiotic and parasite control.ltbrgtConducting the vaccination campaign.ltbrgtConducting the LEGS training in the community.ltbrgtRegarding the MPCA, Samaritan's Purse will distribute MPC for HH assistance which will cover food and any other HH need in the community. The MPCA value for each HH will be determined using the current market price. The basket be comprised of food items, Shelter and WASH non-food items (NFIs) and any other HH needs. A total of 5,000 HHs will be targeted under this program. The MPCA modality will speed up the availability of food and other needed supplies for the beneficiaries through exchange of cash on the local market. Cash Management committees will be selected for each payam in order to assist the project team with mobilization of the beneficiaries, crowd control and maintaining order on the distribution days. A post distribution monitoring exercise will be conducted to better understand spending patterns and unmet needs.ltbrgtSamaritan’s Purse is currently running a Multi sectoral programme funded by SHF in BNS. In the Nutrition sector, Samaritan’s Purse is conducting nutrition screening for children under 5 and PLW. The selection criteria for the FSL and MPCA interventions will include those HHs who have children and women who have been identified as MAM and SAM cases during the MUAC screening exercise. This will enable them to receive further assistance and improve their livelihood means.ltbrgtlt/pgt
